stem: A DHA-licensed nurse is allocated a nonurgent procedure that the nurse has never been trained to perform. What is the best response?

options.text: Ask the patient to accept the additional risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.

options.label: C
options.text: Proceed while a colleague gives instructions by telephone.

options.label: D
options.text: Perform it because a prescriber has requested it.

answerText: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.
rationale: The request does not establish competence. Arranging qualified help protects the patient without abandoning care.

misconceptions.A: Patient agreement cannot replace professional competence.
misconceptions.C: Remote instructions do not establish assessed competence.
misconceptions.D: An order does not extend the nurse’s competence.

pearl: DHA practice: Explain the competence gap and arrange a suitably qualified practitioner.
trap: Remote instructions do not establish assessed competence.

trap: Treating a heard message as a confirmed message.

stem: In a DHA-licensed unit, which activity is the best candidate for delegation to a worker with verified authority and competence for it? The supervising RN has assessed all four patients.

options.label: A
options.text: Choose a new care plan for an acutely breathless patient.

options.label: B
options.text: Decide whether new chest pain can wait for medical review.

options.label: C
options.text: Assist a stable patient with an agreed routine hygiene plan.

options.label: D
options.text: Assess a newly confused patient’s change in condition.

answerText: Assist a stable patient with an agreed routine hygiene plan.
rationale: The routine activity can be matched to verified competence. The other choices require assessment or clinical decisions for new problems.

misconceptions.A: Selecting a new plan involves clinical judgment.
misconceptions.B: The worker should not decide the urgency of new chest pain.
misconceptions.D: A new change in condition requires skilled assessment.

pearl: DHA practice: Assist a stable patient with an agreed routine hygiene plan.
trap: A new change in condition requires skilled assessment.

stem: A nurse in Dubai delegates a stable patient’s planned assisted walk to a competent team member. Which instruction is best?

stem: In Dubai, a new team member volunteers for a clinical activity. Their authorized role is known, but their competence has not been checked. What should the supervisor do?

options.label: A
options.text: Delegate because the worker volunteered without hesitation.

options.label: B
options.text: Delegate and use completion time as the competence check.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask another new employee whether the worker seems confident.

options.label: D
options.text: Verify demonstrated competence for the activity before assigning it.

answerText: Verify demonstrated competence for the activity before assigning it.
rationale: Confidence and willingness are not evidence of ability. Verification should precede the delegation decision.

misconceptions.A: Volunteering does not demonstrate safe performance.
misconceptions.B: Completion speed is not a valid competence assessment.
misconceptions.C: Another person’s impression is not demonstrated competence.

pearl: DHA practice: Verify demonstrated competence for the activity before assigning it.
trap: Volunteering does not demonstrate safe performance.

stem: A Dubai nurse says, “The worker accepted the task, so my supervision ends.” Which response best reflects DHA supervision standards?

options.label: A
options.text: The delegating nurse must maintain appropriate oversight and review the outcome.

options.label: B
options.text: Oversight is needed only when a patient complains.

options.label: C
options.text: Oversight transfers entirely to the receiving worker.

options.label: D
options.text: Oversight is replaced by the worker’s written agreement.

answerText: The delegating nurse must maintain appropriate oversight and review the outcome.
rationale: Delegation requires continuing supervision appropriate to the task. The worker’s own accountability does not remove the delegator’s responsibilities.

misconceptions.B: A complaint is not the threshold for supervision.
misconceptions.C: Both workers retain responsibilities for their own roles.
misconceptions.D: A signature cannot replace clinical oversight.

pearl: DHA practice: The delegating nurse must maintain appropriate oversight and review the outcome.
trap: A complaint is not the threshold for supervision.

stem: In Dubai, a worker assigned to help with a transfer reports no training in the required lifting device. What should the nurse do?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask the worker to follow the picture on the device.

options.label: B
options.text: Proceed if the patient agrees to help with the lift.

options.label: C
options.text: Let the worker learn by trying it on this transfer.

options.label: D
options.text: Arrange trained assistance and training before the worker uses the device.

answerText: Arrange trained assistance and training before the worker uses the device.
rationale: The person and equipment must be matched to verified competence. A patient transfer is not an unsupervised trial of unfamiliar equipment.

misconceptions.A: A picture does not establish competence or safe technique.
misconceptions.B: Patient agreement does not make an untrained lift safe.
misconceptions.C: Trial and error exposes the patient to avoidable injury.

pearl: DHA practice: Arrange trained assistance and training before the worker uses the device.
trap: A picture does not establish competence or safe technique.

stem: A Dubai nurse delegates a permitted glucose check with clear reporting limits. The competent worker reports a result below the agreed limit. What should the nurse do?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait for the next scheduled round to confirm the finding.

options.label: B
options.text: Record the reading without reviewing the patient’s condition.

options.label: C
options.text: Assess the patient promptly and start the indicated treatment pathway.

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the worker to decide whether treatment is necessary.

answerText: Assess the patient promptly and start the indicated treatment pathway.
rationale: An out-of-limit result requires clinical evaluation and action. Delegating the measurement does not delegate away the need to respond.

misconceptions.A: Waiting may allow a low glucose level to worsen.
misconceptions.B: A record alone does not address the abnormal result.
misconceptions.D: The nurse must make or obtain the required clinical decision.

pearl: DHA practice: Assess the patient promptly and start the indicated treatment pathway.
trap: The nurse must make or obtain the required clinical decision.

stem: In Dubai, a nurse is asked to perform an elective procedure outside the nurse’s DHA-authorized role. What is the best response?

answerText: Decline that procedure, explain the scope limit, and arrange an authorized practitioner.
rationale: A request or consent form does not expand professional authority. The patient still needs a safe alternative care arrangement.

misconceptions.B: Seniority does not expand the nurse’s scope.

misconceptions.D: Changing the author of the record does not authorize the action.

stem: A procedure fits a Dubai nurse’s licensed role, but the nurse has no training or assessed competence for it. The situation is nonurgent. What is best?

options.label: B
options.text: Complete the required preparation and competence assessment, with qualified care meanwhile.

options.text: Proceed because broad professional scope is sufficient.

rationale: Broad scope and individual competence are separate requirements. Safe interim care prevents delay while the nurse prepares.

stem: In Dubai, a nurse has reported a patient’s worsening breathing. No effective response occurs, and the patient continues to deteriorate. What is best?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait for the next senior ward round to explain the concern.

options.label: B
options.text: Activate the emergency escalation pathway and continue immediate nursing support.

options.label: C
options.text: Repeat the same routine message and wait for a reply.

options.label: D
options.text: Complete an incident report before requesting further help.

answerText: Activate the emergency escalation pathway and continue immediate nursing support.
rationale: Continuing deterioration needs an effective urgent response. Administrative reporting must not delay the patient’s immediate care.

misconceptions.A: A scheduled round is too late for acute deterioration.
misconceptions.C: An ineffective routine message must not become a waiting loop.
misconceptions.D: The report is secondary to emergency care.

pearl: DHA practice: Activate the emergency escalation pathway and continue immediate nursing support.
trap: An ineffective routine message must not become a waiting loop.

stem: Following escalation of an unresolved care risk in Dubai, which entry best meets the documentation standards?

options.label: A
options.text: A statement that everyone was aware of the problem.

options.label: B
options.text: A list of staff believed to be responsible for the delay.

options.label: C
options.text: A note that an incident form will be completed later.

options.label: D
options.text: Time-stamped observations, contacts, advice, interventions, and the patient’s response.

answerText: Time-stamped observations, contacts, advice, interventions, and the patient’s response.
rationale: The record should allow another clinician to understand the risk and response. Blame and future intentions do not establish what happened.

misconceptions.A: A general awareness claim does not document communication.
misconceptions.B: Attributing blame does not describe assessment or care.
misconceptions.C: A future form does not replace current clinical documentation.

pearl: DHA practice: Time-stamped observations, contacts, advice, interventions, and the patient’s response.
trap: A general awareness claim does not document communication.
